abs.summary: The absolute value of a number: the distance from zero, always positive.

sign.summary: The sign of a number, as -1, 0 or 1.
sign.returns: `num` — `-1` when negative, `0` when zero, `1` when positive.

round.summary: Rounds to the nearest whole number, halves going away from zero.

floor.summary: The largest whole number that is not greater than `x`.
floor.note: It is the one to use to turn a position into block coordinates: `floor(-0.3)` is `-1`, which is the block you are standing in, while `round` would give `0`.

ceil.summary: The smallest whole number that is not smaller than `x`.

params: a number that is not negative
examples:
// distance between two points
math.sqrt((x2 - x1) ^ 2 + (z2 - z1) ^ 2);

fact.summary: The factorial of a whole number: `n * (n-1) * ... * 1`.
params: a whole number that is not negative

relu.summary: The number itself when positive, zero otherwise - the rectifier of neural networks.

number.summary: Converts a value to a number.
params: the value to convert, usually a string
number.returns: `num` — the value read as a number.
number.note: A value that is not a number raises a `TypeMismatchError` with the position of the call: it does not come back as `null` to be discovered three lines further down.

max.summary: The largest of the arguments, or of the elements of a single list.
params: two or more values, or one list

min.summary: The smallest of the arguments, or of the elements of a single list.
params: two or more values, or one list

ln1p.summary: The natural logarithm of `1 + x`, accurate for very small `x`.
ln1p.note: `ln(1 + x)` loses every significant digit when `x` is tiny, because `1 + x` is already `1`. This one does not.

log1p.summary: The logarithm in base 10 of `1 + x`, accurate for very small `x`.

sin.summary: The sine of an angle in radians.

cos.summary: The cosine of an angle in radians.
examples:
// a circle of radius 5 around the origin
for(range(360), block.set([math.cos(math.rad(_)) * 5, 64, math.sin(math.rad(_)) * 5], 'stone'));

tan.summary: The tangent of an angle in radians.

asin.summary: The arc sine: the angle whose sine is `x`.
asin.returns: `num` — the angle in radians, from `-pi/2` to `pi/2`.

acos.summary: The arc cosine: the angle whose cosine is `x`.
acos.returns: `num` — the angle in radians, from `0` to `pi`.

atan.summary: The arc tangent: the angle whose tangent is `x`.
atan.returns: `num` — the angle in radians, from `-pi/2` to `pi/2`.

atan2.summary: The angle of the point `(x, y)` measured from the positive x axis, with the right quadrant.
atan2.returns: `num` — the angle in radians, from `-pi` to `pi`.
examples:
// the yaw pointing from one position to another
math.deg(math.atan2(z2 - z1, x2 - x1)) - 90;
atan2.note: The one to use for directions: `atan(y / x)` cannot tell apart two opposite points and divides by zero on the vertical.

acot.summary: The arc cotangent: the angle whose cotangent is `x`.

cosh.summary: The hyperbolic cosine, `(e^x + e^-x) / 2` - the shape of a hanging chain.

tanh.summary: The hyperbolic tangent: squashes any number into the range -1 to 1.

acosh.returns: `num` — the argument that produces it, not negative.

rad.summary: Converts degrees into radians - what every trigonometric function here wants.

rand.summary: A random number between zero and the limit, or a random element when the argument is a list.
params: a number (upper bound, excluded) or a list to pick from
optional: draws from a generator bound to that seed instead of the shared one
rand.returns: `num` when the limit is a number, otherwise one element of the list.
examples: floor(math.rand(10));               // a whole number from 0 to 9
rand.note: The result is a decimal number: `rand(10)` is not a whole number, put a `floor` around it when you want one.

reset_seed.summary: Restarts the random generator bound to a seed, so the same sequence of draws comes out again.
params: the name of the generator, a number or a string
reset_seed.returns: `num` — how many draws that generator had made before being reset.
examples:
math.reset_seed('test');
math.rand(100, 'test');   // always the same value after a reset
reset_seed.note: It is what makes a test on random code repeatable: reset, run, compare.

perlin.summary: Samples Perlin noise: a value that changes smoothly with the coordinates, the same at the same point.
params: the point to sample; the missing coordinates count as zero
optional: a different seed gives a different landscape
perlin.note: The scale is in the coordinates you pass: dividing them makes the features wider, multiplying makes them noisier.

simplex.summary: Samples simplex noise: like `perlin`, with fewer directional artefacts.
params: optional: the seed of the noise

mandelbrot.summary: How many iterations the point `(x, y)` survives before the Mandelbrot sequence diverges.
mandelbrot.returns: `num` — the iterations reached; the limit means the point is inside the set.

bitwise_and.summary: The bit by bit `and` of two whole numbers: a bit survives only where both have it.
params: the whole numbers, or a single list of them

bitwise_or.summary: The bit by bit `or`: a bit survives where at least one of the two has it.
params: the whole numbers, or a single list of them
examples:
// turning a flag on
flags = math.bitwise_or(flags, 4);

bitwise_xor.summary: The bit by bit exclusive `or`: a bit survives where exactly one of the two has it.
params: the whole numbers, or a single list of them

bitwise_not.summary: Flips every bit of a whole number.
bitwise_not.returns: `num` — `-n - 1`, which is what flipping every bit means in two's complement.

bitwise_shift_left.summary: Shifts the bits to the left, filling with zeros - a multiplication by a power of two.

bitwise_shift_right.summary: Shifts the bits to the right filling with zeros, the sign included.
bitwise_shift_right.returns: `num` — the shifted value, always not negative.
examples: math.bitwise_shift_right(-1, 60);  // 15: the sign bit is shifted too

bitwise_arithmetic_shift_right.summary: Shifts the bits to the right keeping the sign - a division by a power of two, rounded downwards.

bitwise_roll_left.summary: Rotates the bits to the left: what leaves on one side comes back on the other.

bitwise_roll_right.summary: Rotates the bits to the right: what leaves on one side comes back on the other.

bitwise_popcount.summary: How many bits of a whole number are set to one.
bitwise_popcount.returns: `num` — the count of the bits at one.

double_to_long_bits.summary: The bits of a decimal number read as a whole number, without converting the value.
double_to_long_bits.returns: `num` — the same 64 bits, read as a whole number.
double_to_long_bits.note: It is the pair of `long_to_double_bits`: they go back and forth over the same bits, and are how you hash or serialise a decimal without losing a digit.

long_to_double_bits.summary: The bits of a whole number read as a decimal number, without converting the value.
long_to_double_bits.returns: `num` — the same 64 bits, read as a decimal.
